edit.description: Layout::read (~137) binds regions to top-level headings purely positionally via next_heading's cursor advance, with no name/slug check against the slot — so ANY heading-count mismatch (a lone leading title the shallowest-heading read admits, or a missing middle section) shifts every later region's binding by one heading, silently. LayoutReading (or a sibling struct) gains per-region binding data — which heading (if any) a field/prose/collection region actually bound, in document order — for a later region to be judged 'consumed by a mismatched earlier binding' rather than merely empty.

Surface the new per-region binding data as a feature the contract layer can select over (paralleling how derive_layout_rows/layout_unit already surface fields/members), so a coverage-style clause can range over it.

A new shipped default-contract clause, advisory severity (invariant 5), firing whenever a region's actual bound heading (or its absence) does not match the layout's declared position — covering both the title-swallow shape and a missing-section shift — naming the heading that landed in the wrong slot or the slot that never got the heading it expected.

Two regressions: (1) a `prose, field(intent), collection(invariant)` layout over a `# Title` + `##` sections document fires the advisory naming the swallowed heading (GH #45(a)); (2) the same layout over a document missing its `intent` section fires the advisory naming the section that shifted into the wrong slot (GH #44/#41), not just reading the collection silently empty.

summary: A layout's purely positional heading binding silently misassigns every later region when any heading count mismatches expectation — a title swallow or a missing section alike.

tests.asserts: a heading-count mismatch (extra leading title, or a missing declared section) that shifts a later region's binding fires an advisory finding naming the heading involved, in both directions

acceptance: A layout document whose heading count or order does not match the declared regions' positions — whether an extra leading heading (a title) or a missing section — surfaces an advisory finding naming the mismatch, instead of the shifted region(s) reading silently empty or the wrong content landing in a slot.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (cascade adopter probe, GH #45(a)); widened at bf4b4168 (cascade F10 remedy, GH #44/#41) once src/layout.rs confirmed next_heading's cursor is the one shared mechanism behind both symptoms — same fix, not a second entry. Whether a layout admits a document title at all is a separate design fork (`layout-title-heading-admission`), not this fix's job. scoped at bf4b4168

edit.description: KindFacts.registration (183) is typed as readonly Registration[] regardless of locus; narrow it so the embedded and nested-file Locus variants (91-99) type registration as the empty tuple, matching what registration_locus_admissibility (src/admissibility.rs:256) already refuses at runtime.
Regression: a KindDefinition declared with a non-empty registration under an embedded or nested-file locus fails to typecheck.

summary: The SDK's kind type accepts a non-empty registration on an embedded/nested-file locus that the engine refuses at runtime — tsc should catch it first.

tests.asserts: a non-empty registration under an embedded/nested-file locus is a compile error, not a runtime refusal

acceptance: sdk/src/kind.ts's KindFacts type rejects a non-empty registration under embedded or nested-file locus at tsc time; the existing registration_locus_admissibility runtime check stays as the backstop for a bypass.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (cascade, GH #46). representation.md: an embedded/nested-file member 'registers nothing... a non-empty registration is a well-formedness fault' — today only enforced at src/admissibility.rs:256's runtime check, though the SDK's own positioning is that tsc is the first gate. scoped at e1b26728

edit.description: New well-formedness check beside the existing vacuous-clause/unfillable-selection admissibility checks: a layout kind declaring more than one verbatim (non-import) LayoutRegion::Prose region is refused at declaration — a second verbatim prose region can never carry a byte (Layout::read lands the preamble in the first one only, src/layout.rs).
Wire the new diagnostic beside the other admissibility calls.
Regression: a layout declaring two verbatim prose regions refuses loud at admissibility, naming both.

summary: A layout declaring a second verbatim prose region is a permanent no-op today; refuse it loud at admissibility instead.

tests.asserts: a layout with two verbatim prose regions is refused at admissibility, not silently accepted with the trailing region a permanent no-op

acceptance: Declaring a layout with more than one verbatim prose region refuses loud at admissibility time, the same class as an existing vacuous-clause/unfillable-selection refusal.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (cascade F10). Layout::read takes the document preamble into the first verbatim prose region only and no prose region ever consumes a heading, so a trailing declared prose region can never fill. That a layout's prose is preamble-or-import, never interstitial, is already what 0019 states; only the admissibility refusal is new. scoped at e1b26728

edit.description: emit_owned_targets (~3020) decides settings.json is emit-owned via has_registration_members, which calls walk_lock_rows (~2183) — walk_lock_rows_from_doc (~2153) iterates only the LOCK DOCUMENT'S OWN top-level `[[<kind>]]` array-of-tables. A real emitted lock writes hook/installed-plugin/known-marketplace rows nested under `[[declaration.registration]]` (RegistrationRow, Declarations::registrations at ~3113, read back by read_declarations at ~3861), never a top-level `[[hook]]` table — verified on disk against .temper/lock.toml. has_registration_members is therefore always false on a real lock. Derive settings.json's emit-ownership from `read_declarations(workspace_dir)?.registrations` (filtering kind in hook/installed-plugin/known-marketplace) instead of the broken top-level walk.

guard_binds_settings_json_when_registration_members_compose (~1276) forges a top-level `[[hook]]` row emit never produces (source_path/emit_hash columns and all); recut its lock fixture to the real `[[declaration.registration]]` shape a lock actually carries (mirroring .temper/lock.toml's own rows) so the test fails before the fix and passes after.

summary: emit_owned_targets scans only top-level array-of-tables, so real hook/registration rows (nested under declaration.registration) never mark settings.json emit-owned — unguarded everywhere.

per.section: The placements and their enforcement modes

tests.asserts: a lock carrying real declaration.registration hook rows (the shape emit actually writes) makes .claude/settings.json an emit-owned target the guard binds, for both Edit and Write payloads

acceptance: On a harness with a real emitted lock declaring hook/installed-plugin/known-marketplace members, `guard` binds .claude/settings.json at the declared mode; the regression's lock fixture matches the row shape emit_program actually writes, not a forged top-level table.
notes: observed at e1b26728 (cascade GH #40, second half — reproduced on this harness in mode block: `guard .` exits 0 for an Edit or Write to .claude/settings.json). scoped at bf4b4168

edit.description: path_matches (~835) is a `/`-normalized suffix compare with a single-segment rule: for a candidate with no `/` (e.g. the memory kind's root `source_path = "CLAUDE.md"`), the prefix before the match must also contain no `/`, meant to stop `.temper/memory/CLAUDE.md` matching `CLAUDE.md`. But Claude Code always sends an absolute `file_path`, so the prefix before a root match is the repo's own absolute directory, which always contains `/` — a single-segment candidate can therefore never match a real absolute file_path. Relativize `file_path` against the harness root before comparing (a real path compare, never a suffix heuristic) — `guard` (~779) and `manifest_write_findings`'s own path_matches call (~913) both need the root threaded in.

Command::Guard (~327-375) already holds `path` (the harness root); pass it into `install::guard` and `install::manifest_write_findings`/`guarded_manifests` so relativization has a root to compare against.
The one path module `path_matches` should route its relativize-against-root comparison through, rather than install.rs hand-rolling a second string-suffix heuristic beside `normalize_path`.

guard_suffix_path_boundary_rejects_unrelated_deeper_paths (~1334) sends bare relative-looking file_path values (`"CLAUDE.md"`), never the absolute paths Claude Code actually sends, so it never exercised the real bug; rewrite its payloads to absolute paths under `root` and add the case this masked: an absolute write to the real root CLAUDE.md is blocked under mode:block.

summary: guard's path_matches rejects every absolute file_path against a single-segment projection candidate, so mode:block on the root CLAUDE.md placement is cosmetic — it never actually blocks.

per.section: The placements and their enforcement modes

tests.asserts: a PreToolUse payload naming the root CLAUDE.md by its real absolute path is blocked/warned/noted per the declared mode, and the suffix-boundary regression exercises absolute paths, not relative ones

acceptance: A single-segment emit-owned target (the root CLAUDE.md) binds against the absolute file_path Claude Code actually sends, at every enforcement mode; the existing suffix-boundary test is re-cut to absolute paths so it can no longer pass while the real bug is present.
notes: observed at e1b26728 (cascade GH #39). This is the ledger's parked string-path-compare posture rule made concrete — one glob engine / one path module discipline. scoped at bf4b4168

edit.description: manifest_write_findings (~897) validates only the members the pending `content` carries — it never compares against the roster the lock declares for the manifest's collection address, so a write that empties every registration member (e.g. drops all of `hooks.<Event>`) conforms vacuously at every mode. GuardedManifest (~875) or the call needs the lock's expected member keys for its (kind, address) to detect an emit-owned member present in the lock but absent from the pending content, and report it as a finding at the declared mode.

guarded_manifests (~524-570) already holds `&declarations` when building each GuardedManifest; thread the expected-key set (declarations.registrations filtered by kind + manifest + key_path) through from there rather than re-deriving it in install.rs.
New regression: a Write whose content parses as the manifest but omits a hook member the lock declares trips a finding at the declared mode, where today it conforms with zero findings.

summary: A manifest write dropping every declared registration member (e.g. emptying hooks.<Event>) produces no finding — the guard judges only the content it's given, never what the lock expects.

tests.asserts: a represented manifest write that omits a lock-declared registration member is flagged at the declared enforcement mode, not silently conformant

acceptance: manifest_write_findings judges the lock's expected member roster as well as the pending content's members: an emit-owned collection entry the lock declares but the pending write drops is a finding at the declared mode.
notes: observed at e1b26728 (cascade GH #40, first half) — a 0048 conservation instance on the guard: the write represents less than the lock was given. Serialized behind GUARD-PATH-MATCH-ABSOLUTE-SINGLE-SEGMENT: both rewrite manifest_write_findings's signature and its main.rs call site. scoped at bf4b4168

edit.description: Severity (~19) is a closed two-value enum (Error, Warn); Diagnostic (~35) carries no way to mark a warn-severity finding as disclosure rather than a dialable advisory violation. Add the distinction — a third Severity variant, or a `note`/non-violation flag on Diagnostic — that `--deny-advisories` treats as never-blocking while every reporter still prints it.

check (~49) pushes the `coverage.checked` per-kind summary unconditionally at warn severity (its own doc comment: "Returns warn-severity diagnostics only"). Mark it with the new non-violation distinction — it is disclosure (what was checked), never a violation a corpus could tune.

The `--deny-advisories` exit-flip (~250-256) currently promotes ANY warn-severity diagnostic to blocking; it must skip the new non-violation marker so a clean harness's own coverage.checked note never trips it.
New case: a clean represented harness (no contract violations) run with `--deny-advisories` exits zero, though `coverage.checked` is present in the output — the case no existing test asserts.

summary: check --deny-advisories can never pass: the coverage.checked disclosure note is pushed at warn severity unconditionally, and --deny-advisories treats any warn as a blocking violation.

tests.asserts: a clean harness with `check --deny-advisories` exits zero even though the coverage.checked summary is present in the diagnostics

acceptance: `--deny-advisories` promotes only real advisory violations to blocking, never the coverage.checked disclosure note; a clean represented harness exits zero under it.
notes: observed at e1b26728 (cascade GH #42). Intent invariant 5: a shipped coverage clause enters advisory so it is dialable, not so it blocks CI — coverage.checked is disclosure, never a violation. scoped at bf4b4168

edit.description: Declaration rows for a layout source come from exactly two paths: emit over the program's declared members (drift.rs derive_layout_rows) and check's read-time derivation for local-locus kinds only (compose.rs local_document_rows). A discovered committed member of a layout kind that the program never declares is read at check for its field slots (compose.rs layout_unit) and for nothing else: coverage prints `invariant (0)`, explain says "Nested members: none", every leaf address fails, and no finding names the cause. Add a finding, advisory (config.stale posture), when a discovered committed layout-kind member has no matching provenance row in the lock — naming the two remedies: declare it in the program and re-emit, or declare the kind local.
The new finding sits beside config_stale (~2643) — the freshness-fact family the gate already reads disk-vs-lock through — rather than a second comparison mechanism.

Regression: a committed layout-kind document discovery finds but the program's member list omits produces the new advisory finding naming the file and remedy, rather than reading as zero coverage with no explanation.

summary: A committed layout document discovery finds but the program never declares yields no declaration rows anywhere — coverage, explain, and leaf addresses all read silently empty, no finding names why.

tests.asserts: a discovered committed member of a layout kind with no provenance row in the lock surfaces an advisory finding naming the file and the remedy, instead of reading as silent zero coverage

acceptance: check reports a discovered layout-kind member absent from the lock's declaration rows as a named advisory finding; the pipeline.md split (the gate reads declarations from the lock family and nowhere else, local locus excepted) stays intact — the fix is the finding, not new read-time derivation for committed sources.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb, re-filed at d760aa04 (cascade F10, GH #43 as retitled; drained by plan tick ab4a3ead with no entry — re-filed verbatim, now routed). scoped at bf4b4168

edit.description: read_layout_document (~1959, the one reader both emit's committed lowering and check's local-locus derivation share) lowers a Layout::read into LayoutDocumentRows carrying only `nested` and `satisfies` — the verbatim prose region's own span (LayoutReading::prose) and field-section spans are read but never become a row. A layout declaring `prose` after a `collection`/`field` region (a legal, non-first position for the one verbatim prose region) still has the document's leading preamble land there (preamble_taken in layout.rs ~146), with no row or explain surface ever naming which region actually captured it or what it captured.

explain's per-member narration has nothing to read for a layout's prose region span; wire the new row (or feature) in so a layout member's prose content is addressable/visible the same way its fields and members already are.

Regression: a layout with a prose region declared after a collection region still binds the document's preamble to it (existing behavior, per 0019's preamble-or-import rule), and the captured span is now visible via a leaf/row `explain` and the lock can address, not silently dropped.

summary: A layout's verbatim prose region span is read but never becomes a lock row or reaches explain, so an author can't see which region captured the preamble or what it captured.

tests.asserts: a layout's verbatim prose region span reaches an addressable row/leaf, visible to explain, matching how field and collection regions already surface

acceptance: A layout document's verbatim prose region content reaches a row or projection explain can narrate, instead of being read by Layout::read and then dropped on the floor by every downstream consumer.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb, re-filed at d760aa04 (cascade F10 refinement, GH #43). Distinct from LAYOUT-DUPLICATE-PROSE-REGION-REFUSAL (refuses a second prose region at admissibility) and LAYOUT-COLLECTION-MEMBER-OWN-SPAN-LEAF (a collection member's own span) — this is the top-level prose region's own visibility gap. scoped at bf4b4168

edit.description: target_identity (~1593) keys an edge target on a bare `(kind, identity)` pair, splitting `target` on its first `:` — it has no path to accept representation.md's own nested-member address grammar (`<host-address>/<kind>/<key>`). Parse the full address grammar here (host-qualified and bare short forms both), so `resolved_edges` (~1252) and its dangling-diagnostic path both carry the parsed host-qualified identity through to findings.

EdgeField (~55)'s `to` is a target-kind set only; an edge field's entries are free-text addresses at the instance, so the SDK itself needs no schema change — confirm this at scoping and note if a validator narrows what an entry may spell.

explain's edge/finding narration prints a resolved or dangling target's identity; once target_identity carries the parsed host-qualified form, the printed address should show it rather than the bare short form alone.

Regression: two same-keyed nested members under different hosts are each addressable from an edge field via the full `<host-address>/<kind>/<key>` form, resolving to the correct one rather than forcing a rename.

summary: An edge field can't spell a nested target's full host-qualified address — only the bare (kind, identity) short form — so two same-keyed nested members force a rename instead of an address.

tests.asserts: an edge field entry spelling `<host-address>/<kind>/<key>` resolves to that exact nested member, alongside the existing bare `kind:identity` short form

acceptance: target_identity parses the full nested address grammar per representation.md's member section, resolving both bare and host-qualified spellings; explain and findings print the resolved form; the duplicate-key admissibility refusal (NESTED-MEMBER-DUPLICATE-KEY-ADMISSIBILITY) stays the resolver's bar, not the address itself.
notes: observed at f8344d20 (session, plan's 0049 spec-delta pass narrowing its own prior routing). 0049's Decision names every verb accepting one address grammar; its Rejected bullet turns down corpus-unique keys as the address itself. scoped at bf4b4168

edit.description: Audit every admissibility diagnostic's message text: each names the concrete edit (which two clauses collided and the argument that discriminates them, e.g. section_contains's marker) rather than restating lock/contract state alone.
Audit narrate_kind and sibling narration for the same bar — a region binding a heading is named, not only the empty ones (needs the per-region binding data LAYOUT-LOUD-READ-SWALLOWED-REGION adds).
Audit diagnostic construction call sites for the same bar where messages are assembled rather than authored at the diagnostic definition.

summary: Audit admissibility and reader refusal messages so each names the concrete edit an author would make, never only the lock state.

tests.asserts: admissibility and reader refusal messages name the discriminating edit, not just the lock state

acceptance: Every admissibility and reader-narration refusal message names the edit an author would make — the colliding clauses and their discriminator, or the heading each region bound — never the lock state alone.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (John, 09-05 redirect, entry 3 of 4). Every adopter failure in the 09-05 batch shared one shape: the model was right, the message wasn't actionable at the CLI. Depends on LAYOUT-LOUD-READ-SWALLOWED-REGION for the heading-binding data the 'which region bound which heading' bar needs. scoped at e1b26728

edit.description: resolve (209-245) resolves a `kind:` qualifier to Species::Kind(name) with no existence check (244-245), so narrate_kind (476) reports 'no guidance declared' identically for a declared-but-unguided kind and an undeclared one — fold in a contracts.contains_key check so an absent qualified kind name is NotFound (GH #47). Then extend narrate_kind: a layout-content kind prints its regions in declared order plus a skeleton document that fits them; a composed kind prints its admitted embedded kinds and their leaf names.

Regression: explain kind:<undeclared-name> reads NotFound; explain kind:<layout-kind> prints its regions and a fitting skeleton; explain kind:<composed-host-kind> prints its admitted embedded kinds and leaves.

summary: Make explain kind:<x> the adopter's authoring entry point: NotFound for an undeclared kind, a skeleton for a layout kind, admitted embedded kinds for a composed kind.

tests.asserts: explain kind:<x> is the adopter's authoring entry point for every kind shape, and NotFound for an undeclared name

acceptance: explain kind:<x> resolves NotFound for a name no kind declares; for a layout kind it narrates the regions in order plus a skeleton document; for a composed kind it narrates the admitted embedded kinds and their leaves.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (John, 09-05 redirect, entry 4 of 4; GH #47 folded in). Everything an adopter needs to recover from an authoring mistake belongs in explain's own output, never only in specs/. Skeleton richness grows further once LAYOUT-COLLECTION-MEMBER-OWN-SPAN-LEAF lands (not a hard dependency). scoped at e1b26728

edit.description: New well-formedness check: two nested_member rows sharing one (kind, key) across different hosts is refused at admissibility, naming both hosts — mirroring satisfies_label_admissibility's (87) refusal of the same ambiguity for bare fill labels.

member_at (453) and the by_kind pooling it reads assume a corpus-unique (kind, key); confirm resolves/admissibility (137-174) has no independent path that would still silently pick one once the duplicate is refused upstream.
Regression: two hosts each declaring an embedded/layout member of the same kind keyed identically refuse loud at admissibility, naming both hosts.

summary: Two hosts declaring a nested member of the same (kind, key) silently resolve edges to whichever composed last; refuse the duplicate at admissibility instead.

tests.asserts: a duplicate (kind, key) across two hosts refuses at admissibility rather than resolving an edge to whichever composed last

acceptance: Declaring two nested members of the same kind under the same key across different hosts refuses loud at admissibility, naming both hosts; an edge to that key never silently resolves to whichever composed last.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (cascade probe F9, GH #51 duplicate-key half). compose::embedded_member_features/by_kind pools every host's rows of one kind by bare key with last-write-wins; representation.md: 'coincident addresses are a malformed lock.' The corpus-unique key the leaf address grammar already assumes should be enforced, not merely assumed. scoped at e1b26728

edit.description: memberTable (700) indexes top-level composed members only; edgeTargetFacts (255), called unconditionally from resolveMemberLeaves (307) for every embedded value with an edge field, throws when the target is an embedded value elsewhere rather than resolving it. Index embedded values under their kind:key address in the same table (or a joined lookup), with path taken from the owning host's projection.
Regression: an embedded value's edge field naming another host's embedded value resolves target facts and renders, rather than throwing 'resolves to no composed member'.

summary: A render hook cannot cite a nested member: edgeTargetFacts throws on an embedded value naming another host's embedded value, though check resolves and gates it fine.

tests.asserts: an edge field on an embedded value naming a nested (non-top-level) target resolves and renders

acceptance: A render hook on an embedded value whose edge field targets another host's embedded value resolves that target's engine-derived facts (name, address, kind, projection path) and renders, instead of emit refusing outright.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (cascade probe F9/F13, GH #50 widened). There is no 'gates without rendering' fallback: resolveMemberLeaves calls edgeTargetFacts unconditionally, so a nested-to-nested edge is unspellable on the composed half today though the same address resolves and gates fine at check. scoped at e1b26728

edit.description: resolve (209-245) knows only member:/requirement:/kind:/address: qualifiers; add <declared-kind>:<name> as a kind-scoped member lookup — the address form nested_member.host rows, graph.route findings, and mention targets already spell — which also disambiguates same-named members across kinds.
Regression: explain memory:CLAUDE resolves the memory member named CLAUDE rather than falling through to the bare-name path and reading NotFound.

summary: explain does not accept the engine's own <kind>:<name> member address form, though every finding and mention target spells it.

tests.asserts: explain accepts <kind>:<name> as a kind-scoped member address, matching the engine's own address grammar

acceptance: explain <kind>:<name> resolves the named member of that kind, matching representation.md's 'one grammar every row spells and every verb accepts.'
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (cascade probe, GH #49). resolve's qualifier set has no kind-scoped member form though the engine's own findings spell exactly this address everywhere else; a same-named member across two kinds is unaddressable at explain today without it. scoped at e1b26728

edit.description: clause_label (84) folds a section_contains clause's heading in as the field segment (277) and drops the marker, so two section_contains clauses on one kind sharing a heading prefix with different markers compile to one label — fold the marker into the label's field segment so both are addressable, then audit require_sections (which has no distinguishing argument in its label either) for the same gap.
Regression: two section_contains clauses on one kind, same heading, different markers, compile to two distinct labels and both gate independently.

summary: Two section_contains clauses sharing a heading but declaring different markers fold to one compiled label, malforming the lock.

tests.asserts: two section_contains clauses sharing a heading but declaring different markers produce two distinct compiled labels

acceptance: An author can declare 'every invariant carries a Test' and '... a Standard' as two independent section_contains clauses on one kind without them folding into one malformed-lock label.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (cascade probe, GH #48). pipeline.md: 'two rows wearing one label is a malformed lock' — today produced by the compiler itself, not authored duplication. clause() rightly has no label override (the label is compiled, never authored); the fix is the compiled label carrying enough of the predicate's own arguments to stay unique. scoped at e1b26728

edit.description: embeddedMemberValue (461) takes kind: string | KindDefinition<any> and leaves: Record<string, string | Text> untyped against the target kind's own field schema, so an omitted or misspelled leaf typechecks. Make it generic over the kind's T (as kind<T>() already is for MemberInit<T>) so leaves is Record<keyof T, string | Text> with required keys required, when kind is passed as a KindDefinition<T>.
Regression: embeddedMemberValue({ kind: someKindDefinition, leaves: {...} }) fails to typecheck when leaves omits a required key or misspells one.

summary: embeddedMemberValue's leaves are untyped against the target kind's own schema, so an omitted or misspelled leaf typechecks silently.

tests.asserts: embeddedMemberValue's leaves are typed against the passed KindDefinition's own field schema

acceptance: Passing a KindDefinition to embeddedMemberValue types leaves against that kind's own schema at tsc time, required keys required, rather than deferring the check to a factory or a required() clause at check.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (cascade F12). Rides the same 'tsc is the first gate' positioning as KIND-REGISTRATION-EMPTY-EMBEDDED-TYPE — the leaf shape is the one thing a posture kind exists to declare, and only a bare kind: string carries no schema to check against (unavoidable; the KindDefinition path should). scoped at e1b26728

edit.description: read_collection_member (222) takes a LayoutMember's leaves from its immediate sub-headings only, keyed by slug; the paragraph directly under the member's own heading lands nowhere. Land it as a `prose` leaf on LayoutMember.leaves, alongside the sub-heading-keyed spans, matching the name the composed half's embedded values already use for the authored body.
Regression: a layout collection member whose body is `### Title` + a paragraph + `**Test.** ...` (no sub-headings) materializes a non-empty leaves map carrying the paragraph under the `prose` key.

summary: A layout collection member's own paragraph span lands nowhere — not a leaf, not the lock, not explain — while its sub-headings' spans do.

tests.asserts: a layout collection member's own span (the text directly under its heading) lands in its leaves, keyed `prose`

acceptance: A layout collection member's own paragraph (not just its sub-headings) reaches a leaf, addressable and visible to leaf predicates, leaf addresses, and explain, matching the composed half's full-leaves behavior.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (cascade F11, GH #43 leaves gap). A spec whose invariants are H3 + paragraph + bolded marker materializes rows with leaves={} today, so leaf predicates/addresses/explain cannot reach layout content at all while the composed twin carries full leaves — nothing tells the author sub-headings are the leaf syntax. scoped at e1b26728

edit.description: Export a relocation form under a built-in's name (e.g. a `relocate(rule, { edgeFields: [...] })` helper, or `kind({ ...rule.facts, edgeFields: [...] })`) so a consumer can add edge fields to a built-in kind (e.g. `rule`, which must stay at .claude/rules to load) without an `as any` cast that silently drops the edge fact.

overlay_builtin_kind (453) already overlays a same-named row's governs/templates/content onto the built-in (the relocation path) but not edgeFields; extend the overlay to carry edgeFields, keeping row_relocates_builtin's (1091) admission bar (same format, unit shape, registration) unchanged.
Regression: a relocated `rule` kind declaring an added edgeField resolves a graph.route edge and renders it, rather than the field landing in frontmatter with no edge fact.

summary: A built-in kind cannot take an added edge field; the SDK has no sanctioned relocation constructor and an as any cast drops the edge fact silently.

tests.asserts: a relocated built-in kind's added edge field resolves an edge and is not silently dropped

acceptance: A corpus can add an edge field to a built-in kind (e.g. rule) via the sanctioned relocation form and have it resolve a real graph edge, checked at check and rendered at emit — no as any cast needed.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (cascade F13(b), GH #54). representation.md: built-in and user-declared kinds are 'the same construct — ownership, not privilege'; overlay_builtin_kind already honors this for governs/templates/content, not edgeFields, and the SDK exports no relocation constructor to try in the first place. scoped at e1b26728

edit.description: kindsInPlay (351) is first-wins by name (355-356), walking harness.members in authored order — a corpus kind reusing a built-in's name at a different root silently loses to whichever KindFacts value was registered first, with no diagnostic. Refuse two distinct KindFacts values sharing one name, naming both loci — except when the second is a legitimate relocation of the first (BUILTIN-KIND-RELOCATION-EDGE-FIELDS's sanctioned form), which this must recognize and allow.
